claim: Query understanding literature for search engines is organized around identifying search intent, transforming queries, and helping users refine or suggest queries; the book includes query classification, segmentation/tagging, intent understanding, spelling correction, rewriting, autocomplete and suggestion.
locator: Book overview and table of contents; chapters 2–10
notes: Classic IR taxonomy; this article groups it into Understand / Transform / Interact for teaching.

claim: LLM-era query understanding can be framed as interactive query rewriting that makes machine intent explicit and open to user refinement.
notes: Position paper; not a universal production architecture.

claim: Query2doc generates pseudo-documents with few-shot LLM prompting and uses them to expand queries for sparse and dense retrieval.
Query2doc reports 3%–15% BM25 improvements on MS MARCO and TREC DL ad-hoc retrieval datasets in its experimental settings.
notes: Do not generalize the reported range to all datasets or retrievers.

claim: A comprehensive study of generative query/document expansion finds gains are not universal and can diminish or reverse for stronger retrievers due to added noise.
locator: Abstract and experimental overview; Findings of EACL 2024
notes: Peer-reviewed Findings of EACL 2024 version; study covers 11 expansion techniques, 12 datasets and 24 retrieval models.

claim: ICR alternates between generating clarification questions and rewritten queries to iteratively resolve fuzzy expressions in conversational search.
notes: EMNLP 2025; reported on two conversational-search datasets.

claim: LLM-based conversational query understanding emphasizes context-aware intent interpretation, ambiguity resolution, query refinement, proactive query management and multi-turn evaluation.
notes: Tutorial scope, not a single model benchmark.

claim: ReDI decomposes complex queries into subqueries, enriches each with retrieval-oriented interpretations, retrieves independently and fuses results.

A 2026 comparative study evaluates LLMs and traditional methods on query intent prediction, query segmentation and query interpretation, and reports no LLM advantage in intrinsic evaluations; only a few approaches improve end-to-end Robust04 retrieval.
notes: Scope is limited to the three studied tasks and the reported Robust04 retrieval setup; not a universal verdict on all LLM query understanding.

claim: The query-frame schema, pipeline diagrams, conversation-state example and rewrite/expand/decompose comparison are original teaching constructions.
notes: Original diagrams and examples; not reproduced from any cited paper.

claim: The Python demo preserves raw input and marks unsupported or underspecified fields instead of inventing values.
notes: Small deterministic rule demo; not a trained query-understanding model or benchmark reproduction.
